role: Four-layer stack and layer allocation reviewer

directChecks.check: Sum nonzero consecutive planar wire lengths with matching layers; zero terminal stubs and vertical changes excluded
Inner1 ground brep shoelace area: outer ring less all recorded inner rings

Trace centerline partitioned at all relevant polygon boundary intersections; interval midpoint tested against recorded Inner1 void polygons. Runs >0.7 mm retained. This is direct projection, not a return-current field simulation.
Measured Inner1 nonzero routing grouped by source_trace connected_source_net_ids

strengths: Four layers are used rather than forcing every signal through the crowded component layer. Top 1,804.09 mm, Inner2 1,023.16 mm and bottom 923.40 mm carry most planar routing.
A large connected Inner1 ground pour is present: 6,633.61 mm² copper inside a 7,326 mm² outer envelope (90.55% area). Its envelope runs to ±49.5 mm x and ±37 mm y.

Main power routes are predominantly top/bottom, with measured widths including top 3 mm and 2.5 mm conductors; Inner1 signal routing consists of 0.2 mm controls and sensing rather than wide load-current tracks.

Most examined Inner1 point-to-point trunks use reasonable 45-degree paths: measured length/direct endpoint ratios around 1.04–1.15 for INPUT_DVDT, TEC_CLEAR_RAW, MCU_ARM, TEC_CLEAR_N, PD_VALID_N and INPUT_FAULT_N. The geometry is coherent despite its plane cost.

findings.explanation: Inner1 acts as the principal ground-reference layer but also contains 327.93 mm of planar signal routing across nine pcb_trace objects. Their merged antipad/clearance void is a long central slot system. This sacrifices uninterrupted reference under traces on adjacent layers. Measured geometry is certain; noise or functional failure is an inference requiring electrical review. This is not a short.

Two Inner2 LED traces parallel the long clearance slot of the Inner1 TEC_CLEAR controls instead of sitting over ground. D504_A has 29.483406 mm and D505_A has 27.780461 mm of continuous centerline directly above absent Inner1 ground. Their LED function lowers urgency, but this demonstrates that the present layer assignment is not reference-aware. A visual layer crossing here is not a copper short because the traces are on separate layers.

The top-layer TEC_FEEDBACK_PICKUP centerline has a 2.474874 mm direct projection interruption over an Inner1 clearance void between (-0.75,-1) and (1,-2.75). Nearby bottom or top ground may provide an alternate return, which this simple projection check does not evaluate. This sensing/feedback route deserves prioritization over low-speed LED reference repairs. The interruption is measured, while its electrical consequence remains unproven.

TEC_SAFE_EN uses two long Inner1 trunks totaling 124.005444 mm. The longest is 71.656306 mm between (6.1,-17.9) and (-18.75,33), a 1.265 length/direct-distance ratio; the debug branch is 52.349138 mm toward (-37.25,-25), ratio 1.192. These ratios alone are not poor; the concern is spending long ground-plane slots on remote low-speed/debug distribution when the less obstructed perimeter or other signal layers may be usable. No alternate route was collision-checked, so a reduction claim is a proposed improvement, not proof of feasibility.

suspectedShortAssessment.explanation: The attachment shows close apparent crossings/endpoints without a scale or layer/net legend. This role did not run full foreign-net copper overlap checks or localize the crop; no short is confirmed by the layer allocation measurements. The confirmed issues above are missing projected ground reference and routing economy, not copper contact. Dedicated short/clearance reviewers should resolve the attached region.

topImprovements: Reserve Inner1 for continuous GND in the next routing refinement and trial the nine existing Inner1 trunks on Inner2/top/bottom, starting with the long TEC_SAFE_EN debug distribution. Require a real clearance-checked alternate, not an assumed one.

Keep feedback, current-sense and sensor traces over uninterrupted ground. Audit the measured TEC_FEEDBACK_PICKUP reference gap first; route across the slot differently or provide a demonstrable close return path.
Move long LED runs away from matching Inner1 slot corridors; re-plan debug indicators/testpoint placement near their originating nets to reduce cross-board fanout.

Separate reasons for the 433 through-vias: ground stitching is useful, while signal transfers should be counted per net and reduced where a coherent assigned layer can replace repeated detours. Do not simply remove return vias to improve appearance.
limitations: Score is a static layer-allocation score, not the full-board consensus and not manufacturing or bench approval.
No stack dielectric thickness or field solver was used; direct projection gaps do not quantify EMI, capacitance or actual return-current path.
Polygon geometry was read as recorded and processed with double-precision custom line intersection and point-in-polygon code. No external CAD DRC or Gerber check was run.
The 4,078.58 mm metric includes all recorded conductor centerlines, including overlapping same-net branches; it is not unique copper length or an optimized-route lower bound.

Connected_source_net_ids was used for labels. A few source traces with implicit net membership retain their own source trace names; reported critical Inner1 nets and LED/feedback labels have explicit membership.
This review does not establish a foreign-net copper overlap or exclude shorts elsewhere. No board source, runtime or capture was changed.
